name: sus
blurb: Short for suspicious or suspect; made huge by the game Among Us in 2020
title: Sus Meaning: What Does Sus Mean in Slang?
description: Sus is short for suspicious or suspect: something seems off. Long used in slang and hip-hop, it exploded in 2020 through the game Among Us and its memes.
answer: Sus is short for suspicious or suspect: if something is sus, it seems shady, off or not quite right. Wiktionary has the clipping in print from 1972 and labels it slang with African American Vernacular English roots, and it was common in hip-hop before the internet picked it up. It became a worldwide meme in August–September 2020, when players of the game Among Us used it to accuse each other of being the impostor.

body: Sus works as an adjective ("that's sus"), as a quick reply ("sus") and in softer forms like "kinda sus" or the jokey "sussy". It can mean a person might be lying, a deal looks too good to be true, or a sentence sounds unintentionally dirty. Tone is usually light: calling something sus is raising an eyebrow, not making a formal accusation.

ul: "Red was standing right next to the body. Red is sus." (Among Us)
"You've been on your phone smiling all day. Kinda sus."
"Why did you say it like that? Sus."
"Sussy baka": a mock-cute insult mixing sus and Japanese baka (idiot).

body: The Among Us peak has passed, but sus outlived it: it is now ordinary casual English for anyone under about 40, used in texts, comments and real speech. Amogus and sussy survive as ironic jokes. In formal writing you would still say suspicious.

faq.q: Is sus short for suspicious or suspect?
faq.a: Either. It is a clipping that works for both suspicious and suspect, and in practice means something seems off.
No. The word is decades older and was common in slang and hip-hop. Among Us made it a global meme in 2020.
A playful, childlike form of sus. It is mostly used ironically, as in sussy baka.
